status: October 2026 frontier catalog defaults; calibrated 2026-10-19 core plus explicitly provisional 2026-10-27 additions and CC Switch compatibility IDs.

harness_factors.basis: Absolute harness quality on weighted fit and ability. Default 1.0. This does not replace harness_order. That list is a sibling-only preference (same account, model, effort and action): the best sibling keeps its score, and the order flips by work_kind and interaction style. The equivalent coefficient is harness_order_factor = 1 - harness_step * places_behind / (harness_factor * weighted fit and ability), which subtracts exactly harness_step per place.

opportunity_exchange.basis: Quality-versus-quota exchange, and the only rate window_cost reads (via exchange_rate). score_per_displaced_usd is 0.012 score per USD of expected displaced subscription capacity; score_per_displaced_worker_hour is 0.06 score per displaced worker-hour, only when a window has no USD capacity. One score point is about $83.33 of displaced USD, or 16.67 worker-hours. Top-level shortage_loss_per_usd and shortage_loss_per_worker_hour are a deprecated fallback used only when the field here is absent. If both are set and differ, this object wins and the plan warns that the old key was ignored.

subjective.basis: User subjective model ratings (2026-10-21): Gemini 4 Argon leads in divergent/expansive thinking and architectural innovation (formulating schemes, proposing creative research); Claude Opus 5.5 leads in architectural landing rigor and comprehensive global thinking; GPT 6.1 Sol lacks global vision (penalized on context_scale=3 / cross-module architecture) but has high concrete module implementation precision (context_scale=1, code_complexity=1..2).

scoring.basis: Ability normally saturates at floor + ability_span (0.6); non-precision frontend uses saturation_span (0.3), and minimum-sufficient tasks get full ability at the floor. Standard routine/hard effort is capped at High; critical, coupled/frontier and high-risk multi-hypothesis work unlock higher effort. High precision earns high_precision_effort_weight times positive effort ability gain above High. Minimum-sufficient work prices excess ability above floor + saturation_span, exempting GUI/frontend at depth >= 2. Opportunity cost includes displaced demand in USD plus smooth weekly scarcity below scarcity_usable_ref_pct. Observed demand behind schedule is floored at demand_pace_floor_ratio times linear pace. Near weekly reset, surplus earns reset_bonus_max and discounts overqualification. Fast-capable models (Sol/Astra) enable fast mode (2x burn) during pre-reset sprints (sunk_weight >= fast_sprint_sunk_threshold) or when speed is requested and usable quota after 2x burn remains >= fast_plentiful_usable_pct.

models.usd_basis: `usd_per_hour`: API list price (platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing, developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing; cache reads and writes priced separately) of the tokens one active session-hour spent, from 14 days of local session logs to 2026-10-12, pooled over efforts (the hourly spend barely moves with effort; a higher effort runs longer instead): Opus 5.5 $7.5 (131 h), Sonnet 5.5 $4.4 (54 h), Sol 6.1 $2.6 (396 h), Astra $22.6 (89 h). Fable has no history: Opus times the 2.5x list-price ratio. Recompute from usage-stats.json when prices or models change.
models.capabilities_basis: 6D vectors: benchmark-calibrated core rows retain their existing basis; newly discovered frontier rows use explicitly provisional routing priors, not measured benchmark scores. Visual/GUI zero for text-only catalog entries. Full catalog evidence and compatibility policy: model-capabilities.md (2026-10-27).
models.basis: Absolute tiers (at High effort) are provisional: derived from the ordering already in model-capabilities.md (Grok behind the leaders, Flash by user preference) and the user's ratings. Stated by the user 2026-10-09 and updated 2026-10-14 with Gemini 4 Argon: absolute ability order Opus > Astra > Argon > Sonnet > Sol > Grok > Flash; Dot is Astra (the user told me to treat it so, and OpenAI documents Dot as Astra-powered), so it has Astra's tier, meets every difficulty floor and has unlimited usage. User 2026-10-09: Dot is not limited to text; it has its own computer and can receive code, public data and handed-over tables and return files, so it is a candidate for every route unless the parent marks the work `needs.local_only` (`excluded_when: local_only`) or it needs vision; visual ability Opus 5.5 > Astra > Argon > Sol > Sonnet > Flash (the numeric `visual` values 1.0/0.8/0.75/0.7/0.6/0.3 encode that order; false means no vision). Argon shares the Antigravity Gemini pool with Flash but burns roughly 8x as much quota per hour (`burn_pct_per_worker_hour`). Fable is on hold. Correct the rest here; nothing else encodes a global ranking.
models.order_basis: Zero-to-frontier-ceiling normalization over AA v4.3.2 (2026-10-19), Bug Hunt Bench (n=2..5 runs), Terminal-Bench 2.0/4.0, Mercor BrowseComp, MMMU-Pro, OSWorld/GUI harness grounding, and 14d local usage-stats.json.

effort_curves.basis: Per-model effort curves, 2026-10-09. `ability` is the change in tier from High: the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index change from High at each effort (independent; leaderboard of that date) times 0.1 tier per index point (for Opus that reproduces the policy-wide curve at medium, xhigh and max). `burn` is the burn multiplier: 0.7 (the policy-wide value for High) times Artificial Analysis cost per task relative to High, so it carries the longer runs higher efforts need. Efforts a model has no entry for fall back to the policy-wide `effort_ability` and `effort_burn`. Grok has no medium or max entry, Flash no low, xhigh or max. Fable and Dot use the policy-wide curve.
